findings.diagnosis: The prompt under-protects predicate–complement attachments: it permits cuts that separate a verb/auxiliary/copula from the essential complement (object, PP, numeral/parenthetical, or named-location) that completes its meaning, producing contradictions or orphan fragments when pieces are translated independently.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_44','en_us_1650','en_us_375','en_us_101','en_us_1617','en_us_1062','en_us_1567','en_us_1570','en_us_156','en_us_733'] — these sentences all place a finite verb or copula whose required complement (a prepositional phrase, object NP, numeral/parenthetical unit, or named-location phrase) appears later in the sentence; the prompt allows cuts between the predicate and that complement, creating high-contradiction/orphan fragments.
findings.type_predicate: Sentences where a finite verb (including auxiliaries or copulas) or clear verbal predicate is followed later in the same sentence by an essential complement that supplies location, time, measure, object, a parenthetical/numeric unit, or a named-entity argument.

edit.text: Do not cut between a finite verb (including auxiliaries/copulas) and its required complement: objects, PPs giving location/time/measure, numeral/parenthetical units, or named-location/name arguments.
